predictions.text: For control mail a delivered file has exactly one X-Pm-Internal-Id and one X-Pm-Gluon-Id, the Gluon field topmost. S1 and S4 permit duplicates elsewhere.

Internal-ID: forged X-Pm-Internal-Id fields do not survive into A's delivered file, per route (B's Bridge SMTP, C's smtplib, A to its second address), preserving S1's keep branch; duplicates counted without attributing cause. Gluon-ID: a hypothesis (unknown), judged separately. A route that does not preserve the submitted fields is unobservable for P2.
A message's Proton ID is equal before and after a move, label add or remove, archive, trash and restore, and a flag change; compared separately from the Gluon ID.
A draft edit and replacement changes the ID at replacement and keeps it after send; Proton and Gluon IDs compared separately.
Re-importing identical content creates a distinct Proton message each time, for literals carrying no existing Gluon ID; one naming an existing message's Gluon ID reuses it (S9, H11d).
Frozen separately per G7 step, comparing Proton ID, Gluon ID, UID, UIDVALIDITY and bytes independently; each step's baseline is the state the previous step left.
Hypothesis (no source): after account re-add the Proton IDs are unchanged and UIDVALIDITY is not.
Hypothesis (no source): split and combined address mode serve the same Proton ID for the same message.

A message in several labels appears once per label folder under one ID; header-only observation reads set no flag. Cost is a measurement, comparable to H10 only if a cold pass is proved by counted connector fetches.
Hypothesis (no source): a move racing a header-only scan gives, per message, the old membership, the new, or both, never neither, and never a changed Proton ID; the achieved overlap is counted.

On multipart fixtures, retained incremental files equal Bridge's served bytes apart from the documented LF endings and one X-TUID field (the P11 method), against the contemporaneous served bytes and fresh downloads.
Every policy branch is tested locally; live, ordinary folders give only no_acceptance_rule and Recovered Messages gives recovered_folder.
